name: Warm Garden Portraits — reference look
intended_use: Machine-readable reference analysis and an estimated creative look for a custom application developing Fujifilm RAF files.

status.pixel_measurements: Measured from the four supplied finished JPEGs after decoding to sRGB.
status.creative_parameters: Manually estimated from visual appearance; these are newly designed settings, not recovered original settings.
status.validation: JSON structure and numeric ranges checked. No source RAF or neutral before-image was supplied, so the creative transform has not been matched or validated on RAW photographs.
status.compatibility: Custom application contract. Not a Lightroom, Capture One, camera recipe, XMP preset, or directly importable vendor preset.

appearance.overall: Bright, warm environmental portraits with strong color separation and moderate contrast.
appearance.exposure: Bright clothing and readable faces against considerably darker vegetation and ironwork; overall histogram varies strongly with composition.
appearance.white_balance: White garments appear neutral to slightly cool, while skin and stone remain warm. Preserve this separation rather than warming the whole image heavily.
appearance.tone: Deep shadow separation, a subtle raised black endpoint, slightly lifted middle and upper-middle tones, and a gentle highlight shoulder.
appearance.skin: Warm peach and copper hues. Preserve the subject's actual skin color; do not force all subjects to these reference samples.
appearance.greens: Rich forest and olive greens, often dark; warmer foliage where lit.
appearance.blues: Denim leans toward cyan-blue, with visible fabric texture.
appearance.reds: Distinct red flowers and copper-red hair with strong saturation.
appearance.microcontrast: Moderately crisp detail with smooth portrait rendering; no obvious heavy clarity or dehaze effect.
appearance.grain: No reliable intentional grain signature can be separated from JPEG compression and resizing.
appearance.light: Soft outdoor light with subject/background separation and warmer practical lamps; lighting is part of the look and cannot be recreated by a global preset alone.

unknown_original_settings.reason: No EXIF or standard XMP signature was found in the supplied files. Finished image pixels do not uniquely determine capture settings, white balance, tone curves, local edits, or a RAW development profile. The source camera is not known to be Fujifilm.

raw_development_contract.input: Fujifilm RAF; read camera model, sensor pattern, black/white levels and color metadata from each file.
raw_development_contract.sensor_note: Support the actual Bayer or X-Trans layout reported by the camera; do not assume every RAF is X-Trans.
raw_development_contract.baseline: Use a consistent, documented neutral/default RAW rendering with camera-appropriate color conversion. A change of baseline changes the appearance of this look.
raw_development_contract.film_simulation: No original film simulation can be identified. Do not assume a Fuji film simulation was used. Avoid stacking an unrelated stylized baseline beneath this look.
raw_development_contract.recommended_precision: At least float32 through color and tone operations; avoid 8-bit intermediate processing.

exposure_ev.formula: Multiply scene-linear RAW-derived RGB by 2^exposure_ev before the baseline display tone map.
exposure_ev.auto_estimation: Off by default. Adjust for the new scene and subject; do not match the whole reference histogram blindly.

white_balance.policy: Start from camera as-shot multipliers, or a user-selected neutral patch. Apply the RAW engine's camera-specific white balance before the creative look.
white_balance.reason: Kelvin/tint and camera RGB multipliers cannot be inferred reliably from these JPEGs and are not transferable without the target camera calibration.

highlight_reconstruction.policy: Use the RAW engine's supported reconstruction when channels clip; inspect white clothing.

noise_reduction.policy: Adapt to sensor and ISO; no fixed amount is inferred.

demosaic_and_detail.policy: Use camera-appropriate demosaicing; evaluate fine foliage and fabric at 100 percent.

lens_corrections.policy: Use available camera/lens metadata and the user's preference.

handoff_to_creative_pipeline.image_state: Already demosaiced, white-balanced, exposure-adjusted and baseline tone-mapped.
handoff_to_creative_pipeline.color_space: sRGB primaries, D65 white, standard sRGB transfer function
handoff_to_creative_pipeline.important: The creative curves operate on display-encoded sRGB, not linear sensor RGB, log RGB, Adobe RGB, or ACES. Convert explicitly at the handoff.

estimated_creative_pipeline.provenance: Estimated design, not a measured inverse transfer function.
estimated_creative_pipeline.confidence: Medium for the broad visual direction; low for exact numeric match on an unseen RAF.

hsl_sector_adjustments.color_model: Standard cylindrical HSL calculated from encoded sRGB; hue in degrees, saturation and lightness in [0,1]. This is not HSV.
hsl_sector_adjustments.interpolation: Piecewise linear interpolation of each parameter over circular hue. Interpolate from the 300-degree anchor to a duplicate of the 0-degree anchor at 360. Evaluate all sector parameters using the original H, S, L.

neutral_protection.effect: All sector changes fade to zero on near-neutral pixels.

application_formulas.lightness: Let d = w * interpolated_lightness_adjustment. L_out = L + d*(1-L) if d>=0, otherwise L_out = L + d*L. Clamp to [0,1].
application_formulas.conversion: Convert the adjusted HSL triplet back to encoded sRGB.

hsl_sector_adjustments.intent: Favor cyan-blue denim, slightly warmer and darker foliage, and warm skin without globally saturating the frame. The same hue values in unrelated objects will also change.

master_rgb_tone_curve.application: Apply the same scalar curve independently to R, G and B.
master_rgb_tone_curve.interpolation: Piecewise linear; clamp outside the tabulated input range to the corresponding endpoint. Use this interpolation for reproducible version-1 rendering.
master_rgb_tone_curve.intent: Very subtle lifted floor, deeper low tones, brighter middle tones and compressed top highlights.
master_rgb_tone_curve.important: This curve is a forward creative transform for a neutral baseline. It is not the source photographer's recovered curve. Applying it to the finished reference JPEGs would grade them again.

per_channel_tone_curves.space: Encoded sRGB after the master curve
per_channel_tone_curves.intent: Very mild cool bias in shadows and warm bias through middle and upper tones; retain near-neutral white endpoints.
per_channel_tone_curves.color_grading_note: This is the executable color-tone adjustment. Do not also apply a second split-toning operation from the descriptive appearance notes.

global_hsl_saturation.formula: After the RGB curves, convert encoded RGB to standard HSL, set S=clamp(0.98*S,0,1), preserve H and L, and convert back to encoded RGB.

strength_blend_linear_srgb.formula: Decode both original pipeline input and fully graded RGB with the sRGB inverse transfer function; out_linear=(1-strength)*input_linear+strength*graded_linear; encode with the sRGB forward transfer function.
strength_blend_linear_srgb.strength_zero: Identity relative to the creative-pipeline input; RAW exposure, white balance and baseline rendering remain separate.

srgb_transfer_functions.output: Clamp final output to [0,1] for SDR sRGB export, then quantize only at export.

clarity.reason: No reliable amount can be separated from optics, lighting and JPEG rendering.

sharpening.reason: Treat RAW detail and final-size output sharpening separately; no exact radius or amount can be recovered.

highlight_and_shadow_design.execution: Already encoded in the master and channel curves; these notes are not additional processing stages.

black_floor.intent: Subtle floor lift rather than a strong faded matte look.

deep_shadows.intent: Retain deep foliage and background ironwork.

highlight_shoulder.intent: Soften the brightest rendered values while maintaining bright white clothing.

highlight_and_shadow_design.raw_highlight_recovery: Separate upstream RAW operation; this display curve cannot restore channels already clipped in the baseline render.

measurement_contract.source_decoder: macOS ImageIO / CoreGraphics rendered into 8-bit sRGB RGBA; alpha discarded.
measurement_contract.coordinates: Pixel XY on the full 1440x1800 JPEG, origin at top left. Bounding boxes are [x0,y0,x1,y1], with x1 and y1 exclusive.
measurement_contract.content_bounds: Images 2-4 have approximately [180,90,1260,1710] photographic bounds. Statistics use a further two-pixel inset to avoid border ringing. Image 1 is measured in full.
measurement_contract.encoded_luma: Yprime=0.2126*Rprime+0.7152*Gprime+0.0722*Bprime; an encoded luma proxy, not linear luminance or exposure in stops.
measurement_contract.linear_relative_luminance: Decode sRGB first, then Y=0.2126*R+0.7152*G+0.0722*B. Reference white is 1. This is relative display luminance, not scene exposure or measured cd/m2.

histograms.encoded_luma: 32 equal bins over normalized [0,1]; fractions of all analyzed content pixels.
histograms.hue: 24 equal 15-degree HSV hue bins from 0 through 360; fractions among pixels with HSV saturation>=0.15 and value between 0.08 and 0.98 inclusive.

measurement_contract.clipping: Fractions refer to decoded JPEG channel codes. JPEG clipping does not establish whether the original RAW sensor clipped.
measurement_contract.material_samples: Manually chosen rectangular samples of visible materials, not calibrated color targets. Median RGB is per channel; median HSV is computed per component over the sampled pixels. Hue at low saturation is unstable.
measurement_contract.weighting: No global aggregate is imposed: reference 1 and reference 2 show substantially the same pose/composition at different crops and are not independent evidence of a second look.
measurement_contract.no_blind_histogram_matching: Content statistics vary with subject area and background. Applying these global distributions to every new RAF would distort unrelated scenes.

reference_variations.description: Tighter full-length crop; most useful for warm stone, cyan denim and deep ironwork. No white canvas border.
Wider full-length presentation with white border. Similar garment colors to reference 1; framing accounts for much of the histogram difference.
Closer portrait with a larger share of dark foliage; lower image-wide median brightness should not be interpreted as a known negative exposure adjustment.
More open greenery, bright white blouse and a darker denim drape. Warm/cool contrast is visible without a heavy global warm white balance.

optional_reference_border.scope: Presentation only, after image processing and resizing. Do not include the border in exposure/color analysis.

presentation.color_managed_export: Embed an sRGB ICC profile for standard SDR JPEG/PNG export; preserve higher precision for intermediate files.

application_guidance: Implement the explicit pipeline order and formulas; creative values are not interchangeable with proprietary editor slider values.
Develop one representative RAF through your chosen baseline, then compare subject tones and garment colors. Tune the profile against that baseline before batch use.
Keep exposure and white balance as per-image controls. Do not force a fixed Kelvin value or exposure offset from these references.
Preserve neutral white clothing. If the face needs more light, prefer a feathered subject adjustment to lifting every shadow in the background.
The custom app may provide user-painted or detected subject masks, but no executable masks or local-edit amounts are inferred here.
Keep sharpening, denoising, lens corrections and output-size sharpening separate from the color look.
To approximate the reference lighting, start with softly lit outdoor portraits. A global color transform cannot recreate depth of field, subject lighting, red hair, flower colors or material texture.
For a numerical match, supply paired neutral RAW renders and desired edited results; a learned or fitted transform requires known input/output pairs.
